description:
FILED s470bk (Opus, 2026-09-05) by the probe that sized #1057's fix
(scratch/s470bk/p1057/alias.pl).  PRE-EXISTING; identical before and after
#1058 + #1057.

    my %h; $h{a}{b} = 1; my $r = \$h{a}{b}; $h{a}{b} = 2; print $$r;
        perl 2      PCL 1        <- SILENT WRONG

The FLAT spelling is right (`$h{a} = 1; $r = \$h{a}; $h{a} = 2` gives 2), and
so is the nested `++` and â since #1057 â the nested `.=`.  Only the plain `=`
over a nested element loses the alias.

THE CAUSE, and it is one line.  `p-setf`'s nested-hash arm expands to
`p-autoviv-set`, whose store is

    (setf (gethash (to-string OUTER-KEY) HASH-VAR) VAL)

a RAW store that REPLACES whatever the slot held â including a live box that
someone else is aliasing.  Every other element write in the runtime goes
through `%p-gethash-store` (docs/boxed-aggregates-design-s455.md 4.1, "an
existing slot BOX is written through â it may be someone's live alias"), and
`p-autoviv-set` is the one entry path that does not.  `p-autoviv-aref-set` is
its array twin and DOES go through `p-array-set`, which writes the box
through â so the two twins already disagree, which is the rule-11 smell that
identifies this as a bug rather than a policy.

WHY #1057 DID NOT FIX IT.  #1057 deliberately did NOT route the compound
assignments through `p-setf`: it binds the vivified container and then stores
with the ordinary `(setf (p-gethash CONT KEY) â¦)`, which honours the write
rule.  That is why `$h{a}{b} .= "y"` answers perl's "xy" while `= ` still
answers wrongly, and it is the measurement that proves the fix belongs in
`p-autoviv-set`.

FIX SHAPE: `p-autoviv-set` stores through `%p-gethash-store` (or simply
`(setf (p-gethash HASH-VAR OUTER-KEY) VAL)`, which is that helper's own entry
point) instead of the raw `(setf (gethash â¦))`.  Check the reason the raw form
was chosen â the `to-string` is already applied, so there may have been a
key-coercion concern; `(setf p-gethash)` applies `to-string` itself.

BAR when taken: the alias probe above plus its array/deref twins, the gate,
and the full sweep (a `cl/` change, invisible to corpus-diff; a write rule
that starts preserving boxes can move any row that aliases a nested element).

=== DONE (s473b) ===
FIXED s473b (Opus, 2026-09-07), commit 3ad7705d, one line.
`p-autoviv-set`'s store went through `%p-gethash-store` like every other
element write (its array twin `p-autoviv-aref-set` already did â the rule-11
disagreement that identified the bug), so a nested `=` writes THROUGH the slot
box and an alias taken before it stays live.
Probes vs perl 5.40.3: the eleven shapes of scratch/s473b/probe/a01..a11
(nested `=` + alias, the flat spelling, `++`/`.=`, deep chains, an array of
hashes, a ref-rooted chain, a numeric key, an undef RHS, a foreach alias) â
all identical.  Guard: Pl/t/autoviv-02.t row 9, inverse-verified on the
782bc37e extraction.  Gate 222 files, sweep TOTAL 18674 (+0), 0 new/0 fixed/
0 LOST.
subject: A plain `=` to a NESTED element REPLACES the slot instead of writing through its box, so an alias taken earlier goes stale (`$h{a}{b}=2` leaves `$$r` at 1)
